title: RFQ restart and replay: a crashed sender resumes the exact signed packet (byte-structurally compared with the pre-crash spool), and a replayed packet yields a duplicate verdict with revision and transcript unchanged

clauses.DACS-3 §8.3.3 (channel message envelope): sequence: number — monotonic per channel, starts at 1.
clauses.DACS-3 §8.12 (replay of offers across se: The channel message envelope includes channelId and sequence (per-channel monotonic). Given CH-6, an offer replayed into a different channel fails signature verification because the channelId differs; replayed in the same channel it duplicates a sequence number and is rejected.
clauses.DACS-3 §8.2 CH-6 (per-session channelId: The substrate MUST derive a per-session-unique channelId, and an orchestrator MUST reject a session that reuses a channelId from a prior session.

spec.honestScope: The quoted clauses prescribe a per-channel monotonic sequence and rejection of a same-channel replayed sequence. They do NOT prescribe a durable outbox, a 'duplicate' verdict string, or an internal revision counter — those are the SDK's restart guarantees (dacs-sdk src/negotiate/durableRfqLifecycle{,StoreFs}.ts) that uphold the clauses, and these vectors pin them as such. Identity, Vet and Listing authority are synthetic fixtures (disposition: verified is asserted, not verified); transport is a local file spool, not the Demos encrypted wire; signatures are local Ed25519 over the SDK envelope hash, not a Demos wire format; the clock is fixed. Packet preservation is asserted by structural comparison of the recovered packet (including its signature value) against the packet durably spooled before the crash; this proves the resumed turn is the identical signed packet, not that no signing call occurred internally.

derivation: Expected checkpoints are derived from the quoted clauses where they reach (monotonic sequences 1..3, exactly one packet for one sequence, same-channel replay rejected) and from the SDK's declared restart guarantees where the clauses are silent (duplicate verdict, revision counter, durable outbox reconciliation) — each cite says which. Every lifecycle action runs in a fresh OS process over the durable store, so every expectation is a restart-survival claim.
fixtures: Two local roles (buyer, seller) with fresh Ed25519 keys per run; negotiable listing bandCenter 10 USDC ±20%; local file-spool transport; fixed synthetic clock; no network, no testnet, no payment, no Demos wire signatures.

vectors.name: crash-after-durable-publish-resumes-exact-packet
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.3.3 (sequence monotonic per channel) means a restarted sender may not emit a new signed turn for an already-used sequence; the SDK's durable-outbox reconciliation upholds this by resuming the exact pre-crash packet, asserted by structural comparison (including the signature value) against the packet spooled before the crash
vectors.scenario: buyer sends the opening offer with an injected crash (exit 86) after the durable spool write, before acknowledgement; the spooled packet is captured; a fresh buyer process then resumes the outbox

vectors.name: same-packet-replay-is-duplicate-no-state-change
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.12: replayed in the same channel it duplicates a sequence number and is rejected. The SDK surfaces the rejection as a duplicate verdict with its revision counter and the full transcript structurally unchanged (SDK restart-guarantee observables, labeled as such)
vectors.scenario: a fresh seller process replays the exact offer packet it has already processed; the full pre-replay status is captured for comparison

vectors.name: full-negotiation-exact-transcript-no-duplicates
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.3.3: sequences are monotonic per channel starting at 1 — after offer, counter and accept (each action in a fresh process) both roles hold exactly the turns offer/counter/accept with sequences 1/2/3, structurally identical transcripts, and one structurally identical dual-signed agreement at the accepted price (agreement finalization observables are SDK surface)
vectors.scenario: seller counters at 9.5, buyer accepts, both roles finalize the agreement; every action is a fresh OS process over the durable stores
